chunks: What al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the sacrificial offering when it becomes disabled before it reaches the place of slaughter: does it suffice on behalf of its owner? He said: If it is voluntary, then let him slaughter it and eat from it, and it has sufficed for him whether it reached the place of slaughter or did not reach it, and there is no compensation upon him. But if it is guaranteed, then he may not eat from it, whether it reached the place of slaughter or did not reach it, and a replacement is due from him.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَ: sufficed and fulfilled the required duty
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial offering designated for hajj
key_terms.تَطَوُّعًا: a voluntary offering not required as an obligation
key_terms.عَطِبَ: became disabled, perished, or was rendered unfit
key_terms.مَضْمُونًا: an offering that is guaranteed or obligatory and thus requires replacement
key_terms.مَكَانُهُ: its replacement or substitute in its place

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a hajj sacrificial animal becomes disabled before reaching the place of slaughter?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling of a sacrificial offering that becomes disabled before reaching the place of slaughter during hajj. If the offering was voluntary, slaughtering it suffices and no replacement is required; if it was an obligatory or guaranteed offering, it does not suffice without replacement, and the owner may not eat from it.
